title: Decision Transformer: Reinforcement Learning via Sequence Modeling
layout_note: A bottom-to-top stack across the full width: a row of circled input tokens (R-hat, s, a for t-1 and t), a row of colour-coded embedding bars, one wide 'causal transformer' band, orange 'linear decoder' boxes only above the state positions, and circled predicted actions on top; ellipses at both ends mark the sequence continuing.
grouping: Grouping by colour per token type: return embeddings blue, state embeddings green, action embeddings yellow-orange, repeated in R-s-a triples; layer names are written in light grey-blue at the right end of each row instead of in boxes.
shapes_depth: Flat: tokens are pale-blue circles with a slate outline and serif letters; embeddings are flat rounded bars with a strong coloured outline and lighter fill; the transformer is one long pale slate band between two dark rules with tick marks at each token position; decoders are orange outlined bars.
proposed_highlight: The whole method is the single wide 'causal transformer' band in large bold serif type; the RL framing is shown by the coloured R-s-a triple pattern and by decoders sitting only above state tokens to emit actions.
lesson: Lay out a sequence model as one wide band over a row of type-coloured token bars, name each row at the right margin in grey, and show one concrete example (a number, a game frame, a joystick) under the last tokens to ground the abstract symbols.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year; no venue printed on the first page of this arXiv version; remembered venue NeurIPS 2021, not verified.

arrangement.units: horizontal rows stacked bottom to top (tokens, embeddings, transformer band, decoders, outputs), unframed except the transformer band
arrangement.inputs_as: circled symbols R-hat_t, s_t, a_t, with concrete examples under the last triple: a grey tile showing the number 21 (return), an Atari game frame (state) and a D-pad with one dark arm (action), each named in grey
arrangement.losses_at: not drawn; predicted a_{t-1}, a_t circles sit above the decoders at the top
arrangement.shared: the linear decoder is drawn as two identical orange bars above the two state positions

taxonomy.task: offline reinforcement learning as return-conditioned sequence modelling

insights.structure: Five horizontal rows stack bottom to top across the full width, with the single 'causal transformer' band in the middle and ellipses on both sides marking an unbounded sequence.
insights.data: Inputs are circled letters in R-s-a order, embeddings are bars coloured by token type (blue return, green state, yellow action), and only the last triple gets concrete thumbnails underneath (a '21' tile, a game frame, a D-pad icon).
insights.emphasis: The transformer is the largest element with bold serif type, and the orange decoders appear only above state tokens, which shows at a glance where actions are predicted.
insights.flow: Straight vertical arrows run bottom-to-top through every column; tick marks on the band's top and bottom rules align each input column with its output.
insights.avoid: Row names ('linear decoder', 'emb. + pos. enc.') are in very light grey at the far right and are easy to miss against the coloured content.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
